newsitem.title: FRANCE: Skiing-French Olympic skier urges crackdown on slopes.
newsitem.headline: Skiing-French Olympic skier urges crackdown on slopes.

text.p: French Olympic medallist Marielle Goitschel called on Thursday for ski slopes to be policed and skiers punished for speeding after two holidaymakers died in skiing collisions in French Alpine resorts last week.
"Ski runs have turned into the Wild West. We need a law," Goitschel, gold medallist in the 1964 and 1968 winter Olympics, told TF1 television.
"We must protect the 95 percent of normal people from the five percent of crazies," she said.

Goitschel, who now runs the Val Thorens resort, has written to President Jacques Chirac proposing that ski instructors act as "police", watching out for hazardous skiing and seizing ski passes from offenders.
The initial reaction from judicial officials was lukewarm.

"Ski runs are free spaces. I don't think we should turn them into roads with policemen standing at every crossroads," said Rene Ternoy, the deputy prosecutor in Albertville, which hosted the 1992 Olympics.
